welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.html:
The Sanish CMS is the private dashboard used to manage everything on the Sanish Laminate website — the product catalogue, the home page, inner pages, the blog, FAQs, navigation menus, and incoming enquiries.

What you can do here

  • Add, edit, and publish products
  • Organise products into categories and collections
  • Build and rearrange the home page and any inner page from a library of ready-made content blocks
  • Manage the blog, the site FAQ list, and navigation menus
  • Review and follow up on website enquiries
  • Control SEO defaults, site branding, and redirects
  • Manage other CMS staff accounts and their access level

Before you start

You'll need:

  • A CMS account (a username/email and password) — see Users & Roles if you need one created
  • Access to the email address on your account, since every login sends a one-time verification code

Where to go next

I want to... Go to
Log in for the first time CMS Login
Understand the screen I land on Dashboard Overview
Understand the sidebar menu Navigation Overview
Understand "Draft" vs "Published" Understanding Statuses
Add my first product Add a Product

getting-started-login.title: CMS Login
getting-started-login.html:
What this does

Signs you in to the dashboard at /cms/. Every login is protected by a two-step process: your password, then a one-time 6-digit code sent to your email.

Before you start

  • Your CMS username or email
  • Your password
  • Access to your email inbox (the verification code is sent there)

Steps

Step 1 — Open the login page

Go to your CMS address, e.g. https://yourdomain.com/cms/ (or http://127.0.0.1:8000/cms/ on a local/staging setup). If you're not signed in, you're redirected straight to Sign In.

Step 2 — Enter your username and password

The sign-in card asks for:

Field Notes
Username or Email Either your CMS username or the email address on your account both work
Password Click the eye icon to reveal what you typed

Click Sign In.

Wrong username or password

If either is wrong, the page reloads with "Invalid username or password." — nothing is sent, and you stay on the sign-in screen.

Step 3 — Enter the verification code

After a correct password, you're taken to Check your email, which tells you which address the code was sent to. A 6-digit Verification Code field and a Verify & Sign In button appear.

  • Open your email, find the code, and enter it.
  • If it doesn't arrive, use Didn't get it? Resend code.
  • A wrong or expired code shows "Incorrect or expired code. Please try again."

Attempt limit

After 5 incorrect codes in a row, the code is invalidated and you're sent back to the sign-in screen to start over.

Step 4 — You're in

A correct code signs you in and takes you to the page you originally tried to reach (or the Dashboard if you came straight to the login page).

Result

You land on the CMS Dashboard with the sidebar visible on the left. See Dashboard Overview next.

Signing out

Use the sign-out option in the top-right of the dashboard header (your account menu) at any time — this ends your session immediately.

getting-started-dashboard.title: Dashboard Overview
getting-started-dashboard.html:
What this does

The Dashboard is the CMS home screen (/cms/) — a single-page summary of catalogue health, pending work, and shortcuts to the most common tasks. It greets you by name (e.g. "Working late? Karya") with a one-line summary of what's happening on the site today.

What's on the page

Stat cards

A row of six counters across the top, each a shortcut ("View all →") to its own section: Products, Categories, Collections, City Pages, Blog Posts, and New Inquiries.

Product Overview

A card showing total products, how many are Published vs Draft, and a published-percentage bar. To its right, a By Collection breakdown lists every Collection with a "total · live" count and a proportional bar — a quick way to spot a collection with no published products.

Needs Attention

A prioritized "things to do" list that only shows items that actually need action:

Item shown Links to Appears when
N new inquiries — "Awaiting first response" Inquiries, filtered to status=new There are new, unactioned enquiries
N draft products — "Not yet published" Products, filtered to status=draft Any product is still a draft
N draft blog posts Blog, filtered to status=draft Any blog post is still a draft
N draft city pages City Pages, filtered to status=draft Any city page is still a draft

If none of these apply, the card shows "All caught up — nothing pending."

Latest Inquiries

The 5 most recent enquiries with status=new, so you can see fresh leads without opening the Leads section.

Quick Actions

One-click shortcuts to the tasks admins reach for most:

  • New Product — "Add to catalog"
  • New City Page — "Single page creator"
  • Bulk City Import — "CSV / Excel"
  • New Blog Post — "Content creation"

Recent Activity

The last 6 entries from the CMS-wide audit trail (who did what, and when) — see Users & Roles → Activity Log.

Result

The Dashboard is a launch pad, not something you edit — every number and shortcut on it links out to the real management screen for that content.

getting-started-navigation.title: Navigation Overview
getting-started-navigation.html:
What this does

The left-hand sidebar is present on every CMS screen. It's split into a fixed set of items, some of which expand into a sub-menu. Your role decides which of these you can actually see and use — see Users & Roles.

The sidebar, top to bottom

Sidebar item Expands to Opens
Dashboard — The home/overview screen
Products All Products, Categories, Collections The product catalogue and its groupings — see Products, Categories, Collections
Applications — The Design Gallery catalogues (S'Shades, Thre3, Cool Colour, Perspective V4, Thermo) that power the live /applications photo gallery
Pages All Pages, Home Page The generic page builder and the dedicated Home Page section editor — see Website Content
City Pages All Pages, Templates, Bulk Import Programmatic local-SEO landing pages — see City Pages
SEO & Settings Site Settings, Theme Settings, Global SEO, SEO Health, Redirects, Schema Generator See SEO & Settings
Forms — The form builder — see Forms
Menus — Header/top-bar/mega-menu/footer navigation — see Menus
Blog — See Blog
FAQs — The single sitewide FAQ list — see FAQs
Leads Inquiries See Leads & Enquiries. Shows a red badge with the count of new inquiries.
Media Library — See Media Library
Users & Roles — See Users & Roles
Help — This full reference (always the last item)

Behavior notes

  • Clicking a group heading (Products, Pages, City Pages, SEO & Settings, Leads) expands/collapses its sub-items in place — it doesn't navigate anywhere itself.
  • The sidebar can be collapsed to icons-only; hovering/expanding it again reveals the text labels.
  • Whichever section you're currently in is highlighted so you always know where you are.

Applications vs. the Applications app

The sidebar's Applications link opens the Design Gallery (the gallery app) — real photo catalogues that power the live /applications page. There is a separate, currently unlinked application_category / application_project case-study feature at /cms/applications/projects/ for written use-case write-ups, which does not have its own sidebar entry. Ask a developer if you need it surfaced.

getting-started-statuses.title: Understanding Statuses
getting-started-statuses.html:
The Draft / Published pattern

Products, Blog Posts, Categories, Collections, and City Pages all share the same two-state status:

Status Meaning
Draft Saved in the CMS, but not shown on the live website. Safe to leave half-finished.
Published Live on the website right now.

There is no "scheduled" or "pending review" state — a record is either Draft or Published, and switching it takes effect on save. A short page cache can delay exactly when the live site reflects it — see the note below.

Products can't publish without an image

A product cannot be saved as Published unless it has at least one gallery image attached. If you try, the CMS silently saves it as Draft instead and shows a message explaining why — this applies both to the product edit form and to CSV import. See Product Images.

The Active / Enabled toggle pattern

A different, simpler pattern is used for things that are either "showing" or "hidden" with no draft state of their own — home page sections, page sections, FAQ entries, menu items, and gallery/catalogue images. These use an Active / Enabled toggle (a switch or a "Hide"/"Show" button) instead of Draft/Published:

State Meaning
On / Active / Enabled Visible on the live site
Off / Inactive / Hidden Kept in the CMS, but not rendered on the live site

A short cache can delay when a change appears

The Home Page/Pages editor states directly: "Changes go live within a few minutes (page cache)." Treat every save in this CMS the same way — reversible and safe, but not always instantaneous on the live site. Give it a few minutes and a hard refresh before troubleshooting further.

Why this matters

  • Toggling something off (or setting it to Draft) is reversible and safe — it doesn't delete anything.
  • Deleting is permanent and, for most content types, cannot be undone from the CMS.
  • When content "disappears" from the live site unexpectedly, checking its status/toggle is the first thing to check — see Troubleshooting → Product not appearing.

products.title: Products — Overview
products.html:
What this does

Products is the full laminate catalogue that powers the storefront's product listing and product detail pages. Everything here is edited from Products → All Products in the sidebar.

Where things live

Task Article
Find a product in the list View, Search & Filter
Create a new product Add a Product
Change, publish, or remove a product Edit, Publish & Delete
What every field on the product form means Product Field Reference
Featured image, gallery, application photo, textures Product Images
Manage the Finish / Design Type / Colour / Badge dropdown lists Managing Attributes
Bulk edit via spreadsheet Import & Export (CSV)

How products relate to other CMS sections

Category ──▶ groups products for storefront filtering (required on every product) Collection ──▶ marketing grouping, e.g. S'Shades, Thre3 (optional) Media Library ──▶ every product image is picked from here Attribute dropdowns ──▶ Finish / Design Type / Colour / Badge are managed centrally, reused by every product

Collections Showcase on the Home Page is separate

The homepage's "Collections Showcase" block does not pull automatically from the real Collections list here — its cards are edited independently inside the Home Page section editor. Renaming a Collection here will not update its card text on the home page. See Home Page Block Reference.

Quick facts

  • A product cannot be published without at least one gallery image — see Product Images.
  • SKU is unique across the whole catalogue and is the primary matching key for CSV import.
  • The product Slug (its URL) is auto-generated from the product name if left blank.

products-browse.title: View, Search & Filter Products
products-browse.html:
What this does

The Products list (Products → All Products) is where you find an existing product before editing it, and where bulk actions and export happen.

The list screen

The page header shows the Products title, a live count of results ("N products"), and three buttons:

Button Action
Export CSV Downloads the currently filtered list as a spreadsheet — see Import & Export
Import Opens the CSV/Excel bulk import tool
+ New Product Opens a blank product form — see Add a Product

Searching

The Search box (placeholder "Name or SKU…") matches against the product name or SKU. Type a term and click Filter.

Filtering

Filter Options
Category Any existing category, or "All"
Collection Any existing collection, or "All"
Status Draft / Published / "All"

Click Filter to apply, or Clear to reset every filter and return to the unfiltered list.

Filters combine

Search text, Category, Collection, and Status all apply together (an AND filter), so you can search "matte" inside just the Draft products of one collection, for example.

Reading the table

Column Shows
checkbox Select for bulk actions
Product Thumbnail (or a placeholder icon if no image), name, and slug
SKU The product code
Category The assigned category name
Collection The assigned collection name, or "—" if none
Status A green Published badge or a yellow Draft badge
Updated Last-saved date
Actions Edit and Delete

The list is paginated at the bottom. If no products match your filters, the table shows "No products found. Create one?" with a link straight to the new-product form.

Bulk actions

Tick one or more row checkboxes (or the header checkbox to select every row currently on the page) to reveal a floating action bar at the bottom of the screen with:

  • Publish — sets every selected product's status to Published
  • Set Draft — sets every selected product's status to Draft
  • Delete Selected

Bulk delete is permanent

Delete Selected hard-deletes every selected product immediately — there is no confirmation undo and no trash/recycle bin. Double-check your selection first.

Next

  • Edit, Publish & Delete a single product
  • Import & Export via CSV

products-add.title: Add a Product
products-add.html:
What this does

Creates a new product in the catalogue.

Before you start

Have ready:

  • Product name and a unique SKU/product code
  • The Category it belongs to (required)
  • At least one product photo, if you intend to publish immediately
  • Any Finish / Design Type / Colour / Badge values you'll need — see Managing Attributes if the value you need doesn't exist yet as an option

Steps

Step 1 — Open Products

Products → All Products in the sidebar.

Step 2 — Click + New Product

Top-right of the product list. This opens a blank New Product form.

Step 3 — Fill in Basic Info

Field Required? Notes
Product Name Yes e.g. "Sanish Premium Matte"
SKU Yes Must be unique across the whole catalogue
Category Yes Choose from existing categories
Collection No Optional marketing grouping

Step 4 — Fill in Surface Attributes

See the full Product Field Reference for what each of these means. In short: Finish, Design Type, Colour, and Badge are picked from managed dropdown lists (with a Manage options link to add a new option inline); Thickness, Dimensions, Surface Type, Product Type, Surface Category, and Application are free-text fields; Accent Colour is a hex colour swatch used on the product's card.

Each of the four fixed spec rows (Surface, Product Type, Finish, Surface Category, Thickness, Dimensions, Application, Design Type) has its own "Show on product page" checkbox — leave it checked to display that row, or uncheck it to hide the row without clearing the value.

You can also add your own Custom Attributes — free title/value pairs (e.g. "Warranty → 10 Years") that appear as extra rows at the bottom of the specs table.

Step 5 — Write the Short Description and Description

Short Description is the one-line summary shown on product cards and the quick-view modal. Description is the full rich-text write-up shown on the product detail page (formatted with the built-in editor toolbar).

Step 6 — Add Features

A simple bullet list of feature strings (e.g. "Scratch resistant") shown on the product page.

Step 7 — Fill in SEO Settings

Meta Title, Meta Description, and Meta Keywords — see Product Field Reference → SEO Settings for length guidance.

Step 8 — Add Product Images

At minimum, add one image under Product Images. See Product Images for the full picture of the Gallery, Application Image, and Texture Variant slots, and how uploading vs. choosing from the Media Library works.

Step 9 — Set the Status and Save

At the top of the form, choose Draft or Published from the status dropdown, then click Save Product.

Can't publish without an image

If you choose Published but haven't added a gallery image yet, the CMS saves the product as Draft anyway and shows: "Can't publish without at least one image — the product would show the placeholder image. Add an image or save as Draft." Add an image and save again to actually publish it.

Result

You're returned to editing the saved product (now titled Edit Product) with a confirmation message: "Product '<name>' created." A Preview button now appears next to the status dropdown, opening a close visual approximation of the live product page in a new tab — see Edit, Publish & Delete → Preview.

Next

  • Product Field Reference — every field, explained
  • Product Images
  • Managing Attributes

products-edit.title: Edit, Publish, Unpublish & Delete a Product
products-edit.html:
Edit a product

Steps

  1. Products → All Products, find the product (see View, Search & Filter).
  2. Click Edit on its row.
  3. The Edit Product form opens — identical layout to Add a Product, pre-filled with the current values.
  4. Make your changes and click Save Product.

Result

A "Product updated." confirmation appears and you stay on the edit form.

Publish or unpublish a single product

There's no separate "Publish" button on a single product — status is just a field on the edit form.

  1. Open the product for editing.
  2. Change the status dropdown (top-right of the form, next to Preview) between Draft and Published.
  3. Click Save Product.

Publishing needs an image

Switching to Published is silently downgraded back to Draft if the product has no gallery image, with an on-screen explanation. See Product Images.

To publish or unpublish several products at once, use the bulk Publish / Set Draft buttons from the product list instead — see View, Search & Filter → Bulk actions.

Preview

Click Preview (next to the status dropdown, only available once a product has been saved at least once) to open a close visual approximation of the live storefront product page in a new tab, with:

  • A floating Preview Mode banner showing the product name and Draft/Published status, and a ← Back to Editor link
  • An SEO Info toggle that slides out a panel with a live Google-style search-result preview and character counters for your Meta Title (green ≤ 50 characters, amber 51–60, red beyond) and Meta Description (green ≤ 140, amber 141–160, red beyond)

Preview is an approximation, not a live mirror

This preview is a separately maintained CMS template built to match the real frontend's layout and styling closely — it is not the actual live page rendering. Treat it as reliable for checking layout and SEO snippets, not as pixel-perfect proof of the live page.

Delete a product

  1. Find the product in the list.
  2. Click Delete on its row.
  3. Confirm the browser prompt: "Delete <name>? This cannot be undone."

Permanent

Deleting a product is immediate and cannot be undone from the CMS. If you only want it off the live site, set its status to Draft instead.

Next

  • Product Field Reference
  • Import & Export (CSV) — for editing many products at once

products-fields.title: Product Field Reference
products-fields.html:
Every field on the Add/Edit Product form, in the order it appears. Only fields that actually exist on the form are listed here.

Basic Info

Field Required? Purpose
Product Name Yes The public-facing product name shown everywhere on the site
SKU Yes The product code. Must be unique across the entire catalogue — used as the matching key for CSV import and shown in the product list
Category Yes Which Category this product belongs to (see Categories) — controls storefront filtering
Collection No Optional marketing grouping (see Collections), e.g. "S'Shades"

Slug (URL) is automatic

The product's URL slug isn't a visible form field — it's generated automatically from the Product Name when the product is first saved, and won't change on later edits unless a developer intervenes.

Surface Attributes

Field Type Notes
Finish Managed dropdown e.g. "High Gloss" — options are shared across every product; click Manage options next to the field to add, reorder, or remove options — see Managing Attributes
Design Type Managed dropdown e.g. Wood / Stone / Fabric / Solid / Metallic
Colour Managed dropdown
Badge Managed dropdown e.g. New / Bestseller / Limited, or left blank for none
Thickness Free text e.g. "1.0mm" — not a managed dropdown, type it directly
Dimensions Free text e.g. "8ft × 4ft (2440 × 1220mm)" — not a managed dropdown
Surface Type Free text e.g. "Decorative Laminate"
Product Type Free text e.g. "Premium Laminate (1mm)" — shown as a tag plus a specs row
Surface Category Free text e.g. "Glossy Surface" — shown as a tag plus a specs row
Accent Colour (hex) Colour/hex The accent colour used on this product's card
Application Free text Comma-separated list of uses, e.g. "Cabinets, Wardrobes, Wall Panels"
Custom Attributes Repeatable key/value pairs Click + Add Field for anything not covered above (e.g. "Warranty → 10 Years"). Each pair becomes an extra row at the bottom of the specs table; removing a row here removes it from the page.

"Show on product page" checkboxes

Surface, Product Type, Finish, Surface Category, Thickness, Dimensions, Application, and Design Type each have their own visibility checkbox next to the field. Unchecking it hides that row from the storefront specs table without clearing the stored value — useful for a spec you want to keep on file but not show publicly. A genuinely blank field is always hidden regardless of the checkbox.

Short Description

A single-line summary (up to 300 characters) shown on product cards and the storefront's quick-view modal.

Description

The full rich-text write-up shown on the product detail page, formatted with the built-in editor toolbar (bold, lists, links, etc.).

Features

A simple list of short feature strings (e.g. "Scratch resistant", "Fire retardant") shown as a bullet/tag list on the product page. Add/remove rows freely.

SEO Settings

Field Notes
Meta Title Aim for roughly 50–60 characters — see the character counter on the Preview SEO panel
Meta Description Aim for roughly 140–160 characters
Meta Keywords Comma-separated, optional — most search engines ignore this today, but it's kept for completeness

An OG Image (used when the product is shared on social media) can also be set — it defaults to the product's featured image if not set separately.

Product Images

See Product Images for the full breakdown of the Gallery, Application Image, and Texture Variants sections, plus External Image URLs and PDF Catalog.

Related Products

Pick other products to show as "You may also like" on this product's page. Optional, no limit enforced.

Fields that exist in the data but are not on this form

Field Where it actually lives
PDF Catalog The product form's "PDF Catalog" panel links to the collection's catalogue PDF (set under Collections) rather than letting you attach a PDF per product directly

products-images.title: Product Images
products-images.html:
What this does

A product can carry images in three distinct slots, all managed from the Product Images area of the product form. Every slot supports two ways of adding a photo:

  • + Upload Images — upload a file directly from your computer (it's added to the Media Library automatically)
  • + Choose from Media Library — opens the shared Media Library picker to reuse an already-uploaded file

Reuse where you can

Uploading through the product form and choosing from the Media Library both add the file to the same shared library — so once a photo is uploaded anywhere, it's available to reuse everywhere without uploading it again.

The three image slots

1. Product Images (gallery)

The main photo set shown on the product's gallery/swatch carousel. You can add as many as you like — there's no maximum. The first image in the list is the Featured image (used as the product's thumbnail everywhere else in the CMS and storefront); use the star icon on any image to promote it to first position.

Required to publish

A product cannot be set to Published without at least one image in this gallery slot. See Understanding Statuses.

2. Application Image

Exactly one image — a photo of the finish applied in a real room/setting, shown just below the product title on the product page.

3. Texture Variants

An unlimited set of close-up texture thumbnails, each with its own editable label (e.g. "Fluted", "Glossy") used as its caption.

External Image URLs (fallback)

Each of the three slots above also has a matching external URL fallback field (a plain image URL instead of a Media Library file):

Slot Fallback field
Gallery External Image URLs
Application Image External Image URL
Texture Variants Each variant has its own external URL option

Media Library always wins

If a slot has both a Media Library image and an external URL fallback set, the Media Library image is used — the external URL is a fallback only for when no Media Library image has been attached to that slot.

Saving behavior

Every time you save the product, the entire set of images for all three slots is rebuilt from what's currently shown on the form — it's a full replace, not an incremental add. If you remove an image from the form and save, it's removed from the product (though the file itself stays in the Media Library for reuse elsewhere).

PDF Catalog

The PDF shown as a downloadable catalogue on this product's listing page is not set per-product — it's inherited from the product's assigned Collection. This panel shows the collection's current PDF for reference; to change it, edit the Collection instead (see Collections).

Next

  • Managing Attributes
  • Import & Export (CSV) — bulk-attaching images by filename convention via Folder Import

products-attributes.title: Managing Attributes
products-attributes.html:
What this does

Four fields on the product form — Finish, Design Type, Colour, and Badge — are dropdowns backed by a shared, reusable list of options rather than free text. Managing these centrally keeps spelling and capitalisation consistent across the whole catalogue (important for CSV import matching and for the storefront's filter UI).

Not every attribute-like field works this way

Thickness and Dimensions look similar but are plain free-text fields, not managed dropdowns — see Product Field Reference.

Adding, reordering, or removing an option

You do this inline, from any product's form — there's no separate "Attributes" screen in the sidebar.

Steps

  1. Open any product for editing (or start a new one).
  2. Next to the Finish, Design Type, Colour, or Badge field, click Manage options.
  3. An inline panel opens showing the current list of options for that attribute.
  4. To add: type the new value into the text box at the bottom and click Add. It's immediately selected on the current product.
  5. To reorder: drag a row by its handle to a new position — this changes the order the options appear in the dropdown everywhere.
  6. To remove: click Remove on a row, and confirm.

Removing an option doesn't touch existing products

Deleting an attribute option only removes it from the dropdown list going forward — any product that already had that value keeps it stored as-is. It just won't be selectable as a fresh choice anymore.

Case-insensitive matching, exact display

Adding a value that already exists (ignoring capitalisation) reuses the existing option rather than creating a near-duplicate — e.g. adding "matte" when "Matte" already exists just selects "Matte".

Why this matters for CSV import

CSV import matches a row's design_type, color, and badge cell against these same managed lists (case-insensitively). A value in your spreadsheet that doesn't match any existing option is rejected as an import error — add it as an option first (via any product's form) if you need a new one. See Import & Export (CSV).

Result

Every product that shows a Finish/Design Type/Colour/Badge dropdown will immediately reflect the change — there's a single shared list per attribute, not one per product.

products-import-export.title: Import & Export (CSV)
products-import-export.html:
What this does

Lets you bulk-edit the catalogue in a spreadsheet instead of one product at a time — export the current list, edit it in Excel/Google Sheets, then import it back. Import also creates new products and can bulk-attach images from a folder of files.

Export

Steps

  1. Products → All Products.
  2. Optionally apply Search / Category / Status filters first — export respects whichever filters are currently applied to the list.
  3. Click Export CSV.

A file named products-export.csv downloads immediately, ordered by SKU.

Collection isn't an export filter

The list screen's Collection filter does not carry over to the export — only Search, Category, and Status do.

Exported columns, in order

id, sku, name, slug, status, category, collection, short_description, description, features, tech_specs, finish, thickness, dimensions, surface, application, product_type, surface_category, design_type, color, badge, accent_color, image_urls, application_image_url, texture_variants, meta_title, meta_description, meta_keywords

Not included in the export: PDF catalogue, OG image, related products, or the created/updated timestamps.

How multi-value cells are formatted

Column Format
category, collection Exported as the slug, not the display name
features, image_urls Joined with " \| " (a space, pipe, space)
tech_specs "Key: value \| Key: value"
texture_variants "Label: url \| Label: url"

Import

Steps

  1. Products → All Products → Import (or Products → All Products → Import from the sidebar submenu — either opens the same screen).
  2. Not sure of the format? Click Download Template for a ready-made sample row with the correct headers.
  3. Choose your .csv or .xlsx file and upload it.
  4. Review the preview: every row is validated and shown with an action — create, update, or skip — plus any error messages, before anything is saved.
  5. If everything looks right, confirm to commit the import.

Nothing is saved until you confirm

The preview step parses and validates your whole file without touching the database. Only the final confirm step actually creates/updates products.

How rows are matched to products (create vs. update)

Import is an upsert — it updates existing products where it can, and creates new ones otherwise:

  1. If the row's id column matches an existing product's ID, that product is updated.
  2. Otherwise, if the row's sku matches an existing product's SKU (case-insensitive), that product is updated.
  3. Otherwise, a new product is created from the row.

Validation rules

A row is skipped entirely (not partially applied) if it fails validation:

Problem Result
Missing sku Row error
Missing name on a brand-new (non-matched) row Row error
category doesn't match an existing category Row error — unless you tick "Create missing categories", which auto-creates a published category from the slug/name
collection doesn't match an existing collection Row error — collections are never auto-created on import
design_type / color / badge doesn't match an existing managed option Row error — add the option first, see Managing Attributes
status isn't draft or published Row error

What happens to blank cells on an update

For most columns, leaving a cell blank on an update row leaves the existing value untouched (it doesn't get cleared). Two exceptions:

  • collection — an explicitly blank cell clears the product's collection.
  • features, tech_specs, image_urls, texture_variants — these are overwritten whenever the column is present at all, even if blank, which clears them.

Publishing rule applies to imports too

A row that resolves to status=published with no images (no image_urls cell and no existing gallery image on that product) is silently downgraded to Draft, exactly like the product form.

Folder Import (bulk-attach images by filename)

A separate mode of the same Import screen: point it at a Media Library folder, and it attaches images to products by matching filenames against the product SKU.

Filename convention

Filename pattern Attached as
<code> (no suffix) Gallery image
<code>-preview, <code>-applied, or <code>-pw Application image

If "create missing" is ticked and a category is selected, this can also auto-create draft products for filenames that don't match any existing SKU — using the filename code as both the new product's SKU and name.

categories.title: Categories
categories.html:
What this does

Categories group products for storefront filtering (e.g. by material type) and can also appear in the site's mega menu. Manage them at Products → Categories.

The list screen

Shows every category with its product count. Actions available per row: Edit, Delete. A + New Category button opens the create form.

Create / Edit a Category

Fields

Field Required? Purpose
Name Yes Category name — slug is auto-generated from this
Description No
Banner Image No Picked from the Media Library
Hero Eyebrow No Small label above the title on the category listing page
Hero Image URL No Overrides the banner image when set
Mega Menu Column No Which mega-menu column this category appears in: "Surface Finishes" / "Panels & Décor" / none
Mega Menu Icon No A single emoji/character shown in the mega menu (defaults to ◈)
Mega Menu Description No Short text shown under the name in the mega menu
Mega Menu Position No Lower numbers sort first
SEO Title No
Meta Description No
Meta Keywords No
OG Image No
Status — Draft / Published

Steps

  1. Products → Categories.
  2. Click + New Category (create) or Edit on an existing row.
  3. Fill in the fields above.
  4. Save.

Assign products to a category

There's no bulk "assign products" screen for categories — a product's category is set from the product's own form (Product Field Reference → Basic Info), or in bulk via CSV import using the category's slug.

Delete a Category

Blocked if products still use it

A category cannot be deleted while any product still references it — the database protects against it. Reassign or delete those products first (or bulk-reassign via CSV import), then delete the category.

Category SEO

The SEO Title, Meta Description, Meta Keywords, and OG Image fields work the same way as on a product — see Product Field Reference → SEO Settings. Only published categories are checked by SEO Health.

collections.title: Collections
collections.html:
What this does

Collections are marketing-led groupings — separate from Categories — used to showcase a themed product range, e.g. S'Shades or Thre3. Manage them at Products → Collections.

The list screen

Shows every collection with its product count. Actions: Edit, Delete. A + New Collection button opens the create form.

Create / Edit a Collection

Fields

Field Required? Purpose
Name Yes Collection name — slug auto-generated
Description No
Images No Multiple images, picked from the Media Library — a Collection can hold several, unlike a Category's single banner
Show in Mega Menu No Boolean toggle
Mega Menu Accent Colour No Hex colour dot shown in the mega menu
Mega Menu Position No Lower numbers sort first
PDF Catalog No The catalogue PDF shown as a download on this collection's product listing pages — this is also what a product's "PDF Catalog" panel displays, since products don't have their own PDF field
SEO Title / Meta Description / Meta Keywords / OG Image No Same pattern as Categories/Products
Status — Draft / Published

Assign products to a collection

Set from the product's own form (its Collection dropdown — optional, see Product Field Reference), or in bulk via CSV import using the collection's slug. There's no bulk-assign screen on the Collection side.

Delete a Collection

Deleting a collection does not delete its products — the FK is nullable, so those products simply lose their collection assignment (their Collection column becomes "—").

Collections Showcase on the Home Page is NOT linked to this list

The home page's "Collections Showcase" block is edited separately inside the Home Page section editor, as its own free-text cards (name/image/category). It does not read from this Collections list — renaming or adding a Collection here has no effect on the homepage showcase. See Home Page Block Reference if you need to change what appears there.

media.title: Media Library
media.html:
What this does

The Media Library (Media Library in the sidebar) is the single shared store for every image, video, and PDF used across the CMS. Any "image" field anywhere — the block builder, product photos, gallery images, logos — opens this same library as a picker. Upload once, reuse everywhere.

Uploading

  1. Click Upload files.
  2. Under Choose images / videos / PDFs, select one or more files from your computer.
  3. Optionally set Add to folder to file them straight into a folder.
  4. Click Upload.

Each uploaded image also gets an automatic WebP copy generated for faster loading (SVGs are skipped, since they can't be rasterised).

Folders

The Folders panel on the left lists every folder (folders can be nested). Type a name into the New folder… box to create one. Folders can be renamed or deleted from the same panel; deleting a folder does not delete the files in it — they fall back to "Uncategorized".

Search & filter

  • Search matches title, alt text, or filename.
  • Type filters to images, videos, or PDFs.

Editing a file

Click any item in the grid to open its detail panel:

Field Purpose
Title / name Internal display name (defaults to the filename)
Alternative text (alt) Accessibility/SEO text describing the image — shown to screen readers and search engines
Caption Short caption text
Description Longer internal note
Folder Move the file into a different folder

Always fill in Alt text

Alt text matters for accessibility and image SEO. Get in the habit of writing a short, accurate description every time you upload — it's one of the checks the SEO Health dashboard doesn't automatically flag for media, so it's easy to forget.

Click Delete permanently in the same panel to remove a file for good.

Permanent, and can break references

Deleting a file here removes it everywhere it's used — any product, block, or page still referencing it will lose that image. Check where a file is used before deleting something that might be in active use.

Bulk actions

Select multiple items in the grid (a bulk toolbar appears) to:

  • Move the selection into a folder
  • Delete the selection

Replacing an image

There's no dedicated "replace" button — to swap an image used somewhere, either:

  • Upload the new file, then go to the place that uses it (the product, block, etc.) and pick the new file from the library instead, or
  • Edit the file's own title/alt/caption in place if you just want to update its metadata, not the actual picture.

"Scan disk" and "Import frontend images"

Two buttons near the top of the screen for bringing in files that exist on disk but aren't yet registered in the library:

Button What it does
Scan disk Registers any file already sitting in the server's media folder that the library doesn't know about yet
Import frontend images Imports images already used by the website's frontend code into the library

Both are safe to click repeatedly — they never overwrite or duplicate a file that's already registered, they only add what's missing.

Image requirements

There's no hard file-size or dimension limit enforced by the form itself. As general guidance for a clean result across the site:

  • Prefer well-lit, consistent-background product photography
  • JPEG/PNG for photos, SVG for icons/logos where possible (note SVGs don't get a WebP conversion)
  • Keep individual files reasonably small (a few MB at most) for fast page loads

Next

  • Product Images
  • Best Practices → Image guidelines

website-content.title: Website Content — Overview
website-content.html:
What this does

Every page on the website — the Home Page and every inner page (About Us, Contact Us, Rewards, and any new page) — is built the same way: as an ordered list of sections, where each section is one block picked from a shared library of ready-made content types (Hero Slider, Rich Text, Feature Cards, FAQ, and so on).

There is no "publish" step separate from saving — changes to a page's sections go live immediately.

The two builders

Builder Sidebar location Manages
Home Page Pages → Home Page The home page's own sections only
All Pages Pages → All Pages Every inner page (About Us, Contact Us, Rewards, and any new page you create)

They share the exact same mechanics (drag to reorder, add/edit/delete a section, toggle visible/hidden) and the same underlying block library — but the set of block types available differs:

  • The Home Page builder offers 9 home-only blocks (Hero Slider, About/Intro, Collections Showcase, Special Edition, Why Us, Applications Gallery, Rewards App, Closing CTA Banner, Editorial/Blog Teaser) plus every generic block below.
  • The All Pages builder offers 15 generic blocks (Page Hero, Content Section, Rich Text, Image + Text, CTA Banner, Feature Cards, Contact Details, FAQ, Testimonials, Image Gallery, Team, Pricing Table, Stats Strip, Logos Strip, Video) — usable on any page, including new ones.

The Home Page's block picker shows some blocks that won't render there

The Home Page's "Add Section" screen currently lists every generic (inner-page) block type as well as the 9 home-only ones. Picking a generic block type like Pricing Table on the Home Page will save without an error, but it will not appear on the live home page — the home page's renderer only understands the 9 home-only blocks plus its own background/anchor settings. If a home page section you added isn't showing up, this is the first thing to check.

How a page is built (the same mechanics everywhere)

  • Add a section — pick a block type from the picker, fill in its fields.
  • Reorder — drag the grip handle on the left of a row; this changes the live order immediately.
  • Toggle a section on/off — hides it from the live site without deleting it (useful for a seasonal banner).
  • Edit or delete — from the same list, any time.

Every section also has:

Field Purpose
Label Internal name shown only in this list — never published
Anchor ID Optional, lets you deep-link to this section, e.g. /about-us#team
Background colour / image / overlay opacity A background applied behind the whole section, available on every block type

Where to go next

Task Article
Edit the home page Home Page Blocks
Every home-only block's fields Home Page Block Reference
Edit About Us / Contact Us / Rewards / Find a Dealer / Privacy Policy / Terms & Conditions / a new page All Pages (Page Builder)
Every generic block's fields Page Block Reference
Bulk local-SEO landing pages, e.g. "Laminates in Mumbai" City Pages

website-content-home-page.title: Home Page Blocks
website-content-home-page.html:
What this does

Manages the ordered stack of blocks that make up the live home page, from Pages → Home Page. The screen's own subtitle sums it up: "Drag to reorder. Toggle visibility, edit content, or add a new block. Changes go live within a few minutes (page cache)."

The list screen

Every current block is listed in render order, each row showing its name, a Hide/Show link, an Edit button, and Delete. A block that's currently hidden carries a grey Hidden badge next to its name.

Add a block

  1. Pages → Home Page.
  2. Click + Add block (top of the screen, next to Preview site).
  3. You land on a picker grid of block-type cards, grouped as Flexible blocks (Rich Text, Image + Text, CTA Banner — meant to be added repeatedly) and Home sections (the rest).
  4. Click a card to open its edit form, pre-filled with sensible defaults.
  5. Fill in the fields (see Home Page Block Reference for exactly what each block asks for) and save.

Only pick a 'Home sections' card here

See Website Content Overview — generic blocks also appear in this picker but silently render nothing on the home page.

Reorder blocks

Drag a row by its grip handle to a new position in the list.

Show / hide a block

Click Hide (or Show, if it's already hidden) on a row to flip its visibility without deleting it. The edit form for a block also has its own "Visible on the site" checkbox that does the same thing.

Changes go live within a few minutes

That's the screen's own wording — reordering, hiding, and editing all take effect on save, but the live site can take a short while to reflect it due to page caching. See Understanding Statuses.

Edit or delete a section

  • Click a section's row to open its edit form.
  • Delete is available from the same list, with a confirmation prompt.

Backgrounds

Every section — regardless of block type — has an optional Background control at the bottom of its edit form:

Field Purpose

Background image Covers the colour; the colour becomes a tint overlay on top of it
Overlay opacity Only shown once a background image is set — controls how strong the colour tint over the image is

Next

website-content-pages.title: All Pages (Page Builder)
website-content-pages.html:
What this does

Manages every inner page on the site — from Pages → All Pages. On this install that currently includes the Home Page itself (listed here too, badged Home editor), About Us, Contact Us, Rewards, Find a Dealer, Privacy Policy, and Terms & Conditions — plus any new page you create.

The list screen

Every page is listed with its title, slug, and block count, plus three controls per row: Preview (opens the live page in a new tab), Publish/Unpublish (toggles the whole page), and Manage blocks (opens its section list — the same drag/add/edit/delete mechanics as Home Page Blocks, just with the generic block library instead).

The Home Page row is a shortcut, not a duplicate

The Home Page row here is badged Home editor — clicking Manage blocks on it takes you to the same dedicated Home Page screen described in Home Page Blocks, not a second, separate editor.

Create a new page

Steps

  1. Pages → All Pages.
  2. Click + New page.
  3. Fill in:
Field Required? Notes
Page title Yes
URL slug No Auto-derived from the title if left blank, with a live preview as you type
Description No An internal CMS note only — never shown publicly
Starter layout No See below
  1. Save.

Starter layouts

Picking a starter layout just pre-fills the new page with a sensible starting set of sections — every block stays fully editable, addable, and removable afterward, exactly like a hand-built page.

Layout Pre-fills
Blank No sections — start from scratch
Landing Page Hero → Content Section → Feature Cards (3 cards) → Testimonials → CTA Banner
About-style Page Hero → Content Section ("Story") → Feature Cards ("Values") → CTA Banner
Services Page Hero → Feature Cards → Pricing → FAQ → CTA Banner
Simple content Page Hero → Content Section

Result

You're taken straight to the new page's section list, ready to fill in the starter blocks (or add your own if you picked Blank).

Add, reorder, edit, delete sections

Identical to the Home Page — see Home Page Blocks for the mechanics; the field content of each block type is documented in Page Block Reference.

Hide an entire page

Click Unpublish on the page's row — separate from any individual block's own toggle — to take the whole page off the live site (it will 404) without deleting it. Click Publish on the same row to bring it back.

Delete a page

System pages can't be deleted

Pages that were seeded with the site (like the original About Us / Contact Us / Rewards) are marked as system pages and can't be deleted from the CMS — only hidden. Pages you create fresh can be deleted normally.

website-content-city-pages.title: City Pages
website-content-city-pages.html:
What this does

Generates programmatic local-SEO landing pages — one per city, e.g. "High Pressure Laminates in Mumbai" — from a reusable Template, either one at a time or in bulk from a spreadsheet. Manage from City Pages in the sidebar.

Two different things are both called 'template' here

  • A Template (under City Pages → Templates) is a saved content layout tied to one product type — it holds the default heading, body copy, why-choose-us points, FAQs, and SEO defaults that every city sharing it will use.
  • The "Starter layout" offered when creating a page under All Pages (Blank/Landing/About-style/Services/Simple content) is a completely different, unrelated concept — a block-builder starting point, not a city-page template.

Templates

City Pages → Templates.

Field Purpose
Name Internal template name
Product type label e.g. "High Pressure Laminates" — used to build each city's URL and to fill placeholders in the copy
URL pattern Default {product}-in-{city} (also supports {state})
Default H1 / Hero heading / Hero description / Main content Support {{city}}, {{state}}, and {{product}} placeholders, automatically filled in per city
Why choose us A list of selling points, shared by every city using this template
FAQs A list of question/answer pairs, shared by every city using this template
Default schema type The structured-data type used for search engines (LocalBusiness / Product / FAQPage / Organization / Article / BreadcrumbList)
Related products Products shown on every page using this template
Gallery Images shown on every page using this template

Create one City Page by hand

  1. City Pages → All Pages → + New (or the Dashboard's New City Page quick action).
  2. Choose the Template.
  3. Enter City and State.
  4. Optionally override any of the template's defaults just for this city (heading, hero copy, main content, why-choose-us, FAQs) — anything left blank falls back to the template.
  5. Fill in SEO fields if you want city-specific search-result snippets: SEO Title, Meta Description, Meta Keywords, Canonical URL, Open Graph and Twitter title/description, OG Image.
  6. Save.

The page's URL slug is generated automatically from the template's URL pattern plus the city/state you entered.

Bulk Import

City Pages → Bulk Import.

Steps

  1. Click Download Template for a ready-made CSV with the correct headers (city, state, product_type, h1_title, hero_heading, meta_description).
  2. Fill in one row per city. Only city, state, and product_type are required — product_type must match an existing Template's Product type label (not case-sensitive).
  3. Upload your .csv or .xlsx file.
  4. Review the preview — it flags rows with a missing city, an unmatched product type, or a slug that would collide with an existing page.
  5. Confirm to commit. All imported pages are created as Draft.

Everything not in your spreadsheet still comes from the Template

Bulk import only sets h1_title, seo_title, and meta_description per row (when provided) — every other piece of content (hero copy, why-choose-us, FAQs) is inherited live from the chosen Template, with {{city}}/{{state}}/{{product}} filled in automatically. Editing the Template later updates every city page using it at once, except for anything a specific city page has explicitly overridden.

Bulk publish, draft, or delete

The City Pages list supports the same checkbox-based bulk actions as Products — select rows, then Publish, Draft, or Delete.

Bulk delete is permanent

As with products, there's no undo.

Editing a menu

  2. Each menu has its own ordered list of items.

Open in new tab Toggle

Active Toggle — inactive items are hidden without deleting

Reorder

Drag to reorder top-level items, or the items inside a dropdown, independently.

Add / edit / delete

Add and edit items (label + link) at either level from the same screen; delete removes an item permanently.

blog-faq-menus-forms.title: Forms
blog-faq-menus-forms.html:
What this does

A generic form builder for any form used on the site (contact, quote request, dealer enquiry, etc.) without a developer, managed from Forms in the sidebar.

Create / Edit a form

Field Notes
Slug The identifier referenced elsewhere, e.g. from a Contact Details block's "Form slug"
Name / Description
Submit button label Defaults to "Submit"
Success message Shown after a successful submission — defaults to "Thank you! We'll be in touch shortly."
Notify emails Comma-separated list of who gets emailed on every submission. If left blank, falls back to the sitewide notify list in Site Settings.
Auto-reply Toggle, plus a subject/body template sent back to the submitter. Supports {{name}}, {{email}}, {{site_name}}, and any field's own name as a token.
Webhook Optional — toggle plus a URL to POST every submission to as JSON (for a CRM, Zapier, Make, or Google Sheets integration), with an optional secret header for verification
Target Where submissions go: a general Submission log (viewed under this form's Submissions tab), or straight into the Leads pipeline (see Leads & Enquiries)
Inquiry type Only used when the target is the Leads pipeline — Contact / Dealer / Architect

Fields on a form

For each field, add:

Field property Notes
Type Text, Email, Phone, Textarea, Number, Dropdown, Radio buttons, Checkbox, or Hidden
Name The machine key the submitted value is stored under
Label / Placeholder / Help text
Required Toggle
Options Only for Dropdown/Radio — the list of choices

No file-upload field type

The field type list does not include a file/attachment upload option — if a form needs to collect a file, that requires developer work.

Submissions

Every form has its own Submissions tab listing everything submitted through it, with the raw field values and which page it was submitted from.

Linking a form into a page

Set a Form's slug into any Contact Details block's "Form slug" field to render that form there instead of the site's built-in enquiry form.

System forms

Forms marked as system forms (used by the site's built-in flows) can't be deleted from the CMS.

seo.title: SEO Overview
seo.html:
What this does

SEO & Settings in the sidebar groups six screens that control how the site appears in search results and how it's branded. This overview covers the SEO-specific concepts that apply everywhere in the CMS; see Site Settings & Theme and SEO Health, Redirects & Schema for the individual screens.

The fields you'll see repeated everywhere

Products, Categories, Collections, Blog Posts, and City Pages all carry the same SEO field pattern:

Field Purpose Guidance
Page Title / Meta Title / SEO Title The blue clickable text in a Google search result Aim for roughly 50–60 characters
Meta Description The grey snippet text under the title in search results Aim for roughly 140–160 characters
Meta Keywords A comma-separated list Optional — most search engines ignore this today
Slug The page's URL Auto-generated from the name/title; changing it later changes the page's live URL, so change with care once a page is indexed
OG Image The image shown when the page is shared on social media Defaults to the item's main image if not set
ALT text On each image, in the Media Library Describes the image for accessibility and image search

SEO Best Practices

  • Write a unique Meta Title and Meta Description for every product, category, and page — don't leave them blank or duplicate them across items.
  • Keep titles and descriptions within the length guidance above so they don't get cut off in search results.
  • Always fill in image Alt text when uploading to the Media Library.
  • Don't change a published page's Slug/URL casually — it breaks any existing links and search rankings pointing at the old address. If you must, set up a Redirect from the old URL to the new one.
  • Run SEO Health periodically to catch products/pages with missing SEO fields.

Next

  • Site Settings & Theme
  • SEO Health, Redirects & Schema

toc.text: The fields you'll see repeated everywhere

seo-settings.title: Site Settings & Theme
seo-settings.html:
Site Settings

SEO & Settings → Site Settings. Sitewide business details used across the site and in structured data.

Group Fields
Brand Site name, tagline, dark/light logo URLs, favicon URL
Contact Primary/secondary phone, primary/secondary email, address (2 lines, city, state, pincode), working hours
Map Map embed URL, latitude, longitude
Social Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Twitter, WhatsApp number
Header / Top bar Top-bar badge text, header CTA label and link
Footer Footer description, copyright line, newsletter signup text
Email (SMTP) Host, port (default 587), username, password (a Gmail App Password is recommended, not your normal password), use-TLS toggle, from-address, and notify emails — who gets emailed on every new website form/enquiry submission by default

SMTP password

Never paste a real personal email password here — use an app-specific password from your email provider. Treat this field like any other credential.

Test before you trust it

After filling in the Email (SMTP) fields, use the Send Test Email button on the same screen to confirm the connection actually works before relying on it for enquiry notifications.

Theme Settings

SEO & Settings → Theme Settings. WordPress-Customizer-style branding controls that feed the site's colours and layout.

Group Fields
Colours Primary, secondary, accent, heading, text, link, link-hover, background, header background, footer background, footer text — all hex values
Typography Heading font, body font (choose from an approved font list), base font size
Buttons Style (solid/outline/ghost/soft), corner radius, hover effect, text colour
Layout Container max width, general corner radius, card shadow style

An approved palette of reference swatches is shown read-only for guidance, regardless of whatever custom colours you set.

Small changes, big reach

Theme Settings affect every page on the site at once — test a colour/font change and check a few different pages before leaving the office for the day.

Next

  • SEO Health, Redirects & Schema

seo-health.title: SEO Health, Redirects & Schema
seo-health.html:
Global SEO

SEO & Settings → Global SEO. Sitewide defaults and integrations.

Field Purpose
Site meta title / description / keywords Fallback used when an individual page doesn't set its own
robots.txt Editable directly — defaults to allowing all crawlers plus a sitemap reference
GA4 code, GTM code, Facebook Pixel code, Clarity code Analytics/tracking integration snippets
Google Search Console verification code Just the verification content, not a full meta tag
reCAPTCHA Off / v2 / v3, with site key, secret key, and (for v3) a minimum score — submissions scoring below the threshold are treated as spam

SEO Health

SEO & Settings → SEO Health (shown in the sidebar with a green status dot). A live dashboard — not something you edit — that scores how completely your published content has its SEO fields filled in.

What's checked Fields scored
Products Meta Title, Meta Description, Meta Keywords, OG Image
Categories / Collections SEO Title, Meta Description, Meta Keywords, OG Image
Blog Posts SEO Title, Meta Description, Meta Keywords, OG Image

It also separately flags:

  • City Pages with both SEO Title and Meta Description blank
  • Published Products with no images
  • Published Products with an empty Description

Only published records are checked — a draft's missing SEO fields won't affect the score.

Use it as a punch list

Run through SEO Health periodically and work down the flagged items rather than trying to keep every field perfect as you go — click Fix on any row to jump straight to that item's edit form.

Redirects

SEO & Settings → Redirects. Use whenever a page's URL changes and old links need to keep working.

Field Notes
Source path The old URL that should redirect
Destination path Where it should go instead
Type 301 Permanent (for a URL that's changed for good) or 302 Temporary
Active Toggle

Set up a redirect before you change a live URL

If you rename a published product/page's slug, do it together with a redirect from the old URL — otherwise anyone with the old link (including search engines) hits a dead page.

Schema Generator

SEO & Settings → Schema Generator. Generates the structured data (JSON-LD) search engines use to understand a page's content, for one of six types:

Type Used for
LocalBusiness A location/city page
Product A product page
FAQPage A page with a list of Q&A
Organization The company itself
Article A blog post
BreadcrumbList The breadcrumb trail on a page

City Pages set their schema type on the Template (or override it per city); products, categories, and blog posts don't need this screen day-to-day since their schema is generated automatically from their own fields.

leads.title: Leads & Enquiries
leads.html:
What this does

Every contact/enquiry form submitted on the live site lands in Leads → Inquiries. A separate, unrelated Dealers directory lives alongside it.

Inquiries

Leads → Inquiries. The sidebar shows a red badge with the count of new inquiries.

Tabs

Tabs across the top filter by which form the enquiry came through: All, then one tab per form currently in use on the site — on this install: Contact Form, Inquiry Popup, Sample Request Form, Collection Inquiry Form. This list reflects whichever forms have actually received submissions, so it can grow as new Forms targeting the Leads pipeline are built and used.

Export

Export CSV, top-right, downloads the currently filtered inquiries as a spreadsheet.

Search & filter

  • Search — matches name or email.
  • Status filter — see the status list below.

Statuses

Status Badge colour Meaning
New Yellow Just came in, not yet actioned
Contacted Blue Someone has reached out
Qualified Green A genuine lead worth pursuing
Closed Grey Done — won, lost, or not relevant

Contact information shown

Each inquiry carries: Name, Email, Phone, Message, City, which page it was submitted from, which form it came through (or "Collection Inquiry Form" for the legacy built-in one), and your own internal notes.

Change a status

Use the status dropdown directly on an inquiry's row and it saves immediately — no separate save button.

Bulk actions

Select multiple inquiries with their checkboxes, then either:

  • Choose a status from the bulk dropdown and click Update Status to apply it to every selected row at once, or
  • Click Delete Selected to remove them permanently.

Bulk delete is permanent

As with products, there's no undo — double-check your selection first.

Internal notes

Add follow-up notes on an inquiry — these are for your team only, never shown to the person who submitted the form.

Dealers

A separate directory of dealer/distributor contacts, managed the same way as any other list (create/edit): name, contact person, email, phone, city/state/address, map coordinates, and an active/inactive status.

Not the same pipeline as Inquiries

Dealers is a standalone contact directory. A dealer enquiry submitted through a form (inquiry type "Dealer") lands in Inquiries, not automatically in this Dealers list — the two are managed independently.

users.title: Users & Roles
users.html:
What this does

Manage CMS staff accounts and their access level from Users & Roles in the sidebar.

Roles

Role Typical access
Super Admin Everything, without restriction
Admin Everything except whatever's reserved strictly for Super Admin
SEO Manager SEO & Settings, plus City Pages (SEO is central to that feature)
Content Manager Blog, FAQs, Media Library, and general content areas
Sales Manager Leads & Enquiries

Roles are additive by design, not exclusive

A role grants access to its own area plus everything a "lower" role can do — e.g. an Admin can also do everything a Content Manager or SEO Manager can. If a sidebar item is missing for a particular login, it's a permission, not a bug — check that account's role.

Create / Edit a user

  1. Users & Roles in the sidebar.
  2. + Add a new account, or Edit an existing one.
  3. Set their username, email (required — this is where their login verification codes are sent, see CMS Login), and role.
  4. Save.

Password / account management

  • A new user's password is set when the account is created (or via a reset flow — check with whoever administers the CMS if you need this enabled).
  • There is no self-service "forgot password" flow visible in the sidebar navigation — if you're locked out, ask a Super Admin/Admin to reset your account.
  • Every login requires a one-time email code in addition to the password — see CMS Login.

Activity Log

The same Users & Roles screen includes an Activity Log — an audit trail of who changed what and when, across the CMS (e.g. "Bulk imported 12 city pages", "Uploaded media", "Scanned media disk"). It's populated by the more significant actions across the CMS (imports, uploads, creates/updates/deletes on the bigger content types) rather than every single field change on every save.

Use it to answer 'who changed this'

If something on the live site looks different than you remember, the Activity Log is the fastest way to see which account touched it and when.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.html:
Login problems

Problem: Can't sign in, or the verification code screen won't accept the code.

Possible cause How to check How to fix
Wrong username/password The form reloads with "Invalid username or password." Re-enter carefully; ask an Admin to reset your password if needed
Code expired or already used "Incorrect or expired code. Please try again." Click Resend code and use the newest one
Too many wrong code attempts You're redirected back to the sign-in screen Sign in again from the start — a new code will be generated
Email delayed No code arrives after a minute or two Use Resend code; check spam; confirm your account's email address is correct with an Admin

When to contact a developer: if Resend code repeatedly fails to deliver anything, or the login page itself won't load.

Image upload problems

Problem: An image won't upload, or doesn't appear after uploading.

Possible cause How to check How to fix
File didn't finish uploading The Media Library grid doesn't show it after upload Re-try the upload; check your connection
Uploaded to the wrong folder Search isn't finding it Use Search (matches title/alt/filename) instead of browsing folders, or check "Uncategorized"
Product images not saved You added images on the product form but didn't click Save Product Re-open the product and re-add the images, then Save

When to contact a developer: if uploads consistently fail with an error message, or files upload but never appear anywhere in the Media Library.

Product not appearing on the live site

Problem: A product exists in the CMS but isn't showing on the storefront.

Possible cause How to check How to fix
Status is Draft Check the status badge/dropdown on the product Set to Published and Save — see Understanding Statuses
No image, so it silently stayed Draft Look for the message "Can't publish without at least one image…" Add a gallery image, then set to Published and Save — see Product Images
Filtered out by category/collection on the storefront Check the product's Category and Collection Confirm they're set correctly and that the Category/Collection itself is Published
Just saved via CSV import and downgraded silently Re-open the imported product The import applies the same "no image → forced Draft" rule as the form — see Import & Export

Product URL / slug issues

Problem: A product's link 404s, or you want to change its URL.

  • The Slug is generated automatically from the Product Name the first time a product is saved and does not update itself if you rename the product later.
  • Changing a slug on a product that's already indexed by search engines or linked elsewhere will break those old links — set up a Redirect from the old URL to the new one when you do this.

Changes not appearing on the live site

Problem: You saved something in the CMS but the website still looks old.

Possible cause How to check How to fix
Section/item is toggled off Check its Active/Enabled toggle Turn it on — see Understanding Statuses
Editing the wrong page/section Double-check you edited the section that's actually visible in that slot Compare the section's Label in the list against what you expect
Browser cache The change should be instant — there's no CMS-side publish delay Hard-refresh the live page (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R)
Home Page block picked from the wrong list You added a generic block type on the Home Page See Website Content Overview — generic blocks don't render there

When to contact a developer: if a change is definitely saved (status Published, toggle on, correct page) and still doesn't appear after a hard refresh — this points to a caching layer or deployment issue outside the CMS.

Common validation errors

Message Cause Fix
"Can't publish without at least one image — the product would show the placeholder image. Add an image or save as Draft." Trying to publish a product with no gallery image Add a gallery image
"Delete <name>? This cannot be undone." A delete confirmation, not an error Confirm only if you're sure
A category won't delete Products still reference it Reassign or remove those products first — see Categories → Delete
CSV import row shows an error and is skipped Missing SKU/name, unmatched category/collection/attribute value, or invalid status See Import & Export → Validation rules

When to contact a developer

  • A screen shows a server error page instead of the normal CMS layout
  • A feature described in this Help Center is missing from your sidebar and an Admin confirms your role should have it
  • Uploads or saves fail consistently, not just once
  • You need a brand-new form field type, block type, or menu area that doesn't exist yet

best-practices.title: Best Practices & Checklists
best-practices.html:
Product data guidelines

  • Give every product a unique, meaningful SKU — it's the key used for CSV import matching, so a typo splits one product into two rows on your next import.
  • Use the managed dropdowns (Finish, Design Type, Colour, Badge) instead of trying to type a "close enough" free-text value elsewhere — consistent values are what makes storefront filters and CSV import matching work.
  • Use the "Show on page" checkboxes to hide a spec you're not ready to publish yet, rather than deleting the value.
  • Prefer Custom Attributes over stuffing extra information into the Description for anything that's really a spec (warranty, certification, etc.) — it renders as a proper table row.

Image guidelines

  • Upload through the Media Library (or the product form's Media Library picker) rather than the External URL fallback fields — a Media Library image always takes priority anyway, and it gets an automatic WebP copy for faster loading.
  • Fill in Alt text every time you upload — see Media Library.
  • Keep the first gallery image as your best/cleanest product shot — it's used as the thumbnail everywhere else in the CMS and storefront.
  • Match recommended aspect ratios where given (e.g. Hero Slider's 21:9 vs 16:9) so images aren't cropped awkwardly.

Naming conventions

See Data Rules & Known Inconsistencies for the current, actual convention in use across the catalogue — check there before assuming a format.

SEO guidelines

  • Every published product, category, collection, blog post, and city page should have its own Meta Title and Meta Description — see SEO Overview.
  • Run SEO Health periodically and clear flagged items rather than letting them build up.
  • Set up a Redirect whenever you change a published page's URL.

Publishing checklist — before publishing a product

  • [ ] Product Name checked for typos
  • [ ] SKU checked (unique, matches your internal code sheet)
  • [ ] Category selected
  • [ ] Collection selected (if applicable)
  • [ ] At least one gallery image uploaded, with the best photo first
  • [ ] Application image added (if the product has a "used in a room" shot)
  • [ ] Short Description and full Description checked
  • [ ] Surface Attributes filled in and "Show on page" set correctly for each
  • [ ] Meta Title and Meta Description filled in
  • [ ] Status set to Published
  • [ ] Previewed once before considering it done — see Preview

Publishing checklist — before a bulk CSV import

  • [ ] Downloaded the latest Export as a backup before making bulk changes
  • [ ] Ran the preview step and read every row's action (create/update/skip) and error, before committing
  • [ ] Confirmed any new Finish/Design Type/Colour/Badge values already exist as managed options — see Managing Attributes
  • [ ] Double-checked blank cells won't accidentally clear a collection, features, tech_specs, image_urls, or texture_variants value you meant to keep — see Import & Export → blank cells

data-rules.title: Data Rules & Known Inconsistencies
data-rules.html:
This page documents the current, actual conventions found in the live product data (926 products at the time of writing) — not a proposed standard. Where the data disagrees with itself, that's flagged explicitly rather than silently picking one form.

SKU / Product Code — current conventions in use

Inspecting the real catalogue turned up three different SKU shapes in active use side by side, with no single dominant format:

Pattern Example Approx. share
<4-digit code> <letters> (space-separated) 6395 ZK, 9107 MICRO LINE Largest group
<Letter prefix> <digits> (space-separated) SN 5117, GS 6001 Second largest
<Letter prefix>-<digits> (hyphen-separated) SL-0011, BTM-001, ONH-001 Smaller group

No single consistent format

The catalogue currently mixes space-separated and hyphen-separated codes. This documentation does not recommend changing existing codes — SKU is the primary key CSV import uses to match rows to products, so retroactively reformatting SKUs on published products would need to go hand-in-hand with a careful, verified bulk update (see Import & Export), not a casual edit.

"TX" in product names/codes

At the time of writing, no product's SKU or name contains "TX" anywhere in the live catalogue. If your team previously discussed removing "TX" from product names/URLs, that removal appears to already be reflected in the current data — there is nothing further to strip. If you encounter a "TX" product code in the future, treat it as new/inconsistent data worth flagging rather than an established convention.

"6012UG" vs "6012-UG" style codes

The specific no-separator four-digit-plus-suffix pattern discussed previously (e.g. 6012UG) was not found in the current catalogue in that exact no-space form — the closest real pattern is the space-separated <code> <letters> style above (e.g. 6395 ZK). No hyphenated 6012-UG-style code was found either. If this format is being introduced going forward, it would be a new, fourth convention rather than a continuation of an existing one — worth a deliberate decision (and likely a CSV bulk-rename) rather than an incidental one.

What this means day to day

  • When creating a new product, match the format used by similar existing products in the same range/collection rather than inventing a new shape — check a few sibling SKUs first.
  • Don't "fix" an existing product's SKU format as a side effect of an unrelated edit — a SKU change is effectively a rename and should be deliberate (see Troubleshooting → Product URL / slug issues for the same caution on slugs).
  • If your team formally decides on one standard format going forward, that decision belongs in this document — update it here once made, rather than leaving future admins to guess from inconsistent examples.

landing_html:
Welcome to the help center for the Sanish Laminate content management system (the "CMS" or "dashboard"). This is where the entire public website — products, categories, the home page, inner pages, the blog, FAQs, menus, and enquiries — is managed. There is no manual "publish" step for most content: saving a change goes live on its own.

Changes can take a few minutes to appear

The website's Home Page/Pages screen states this directly: "Changes go live within a few minutes (page cache)." Saving isn't instant on every screen — a short cache delay is normal. If a change doesn't appear right away, wait a few minutes and hard-refresh before assuming something's wrong — see Troubleshooting → Changes not appearing.

This documentation is written for the people who use the CMS day to day — not developers. Every page describes exactly what you'll see on screen, using the same labels and buttons as the real dashboard.

New here?

Start with Getting Started — it covers logging in, the dashboard layout, and what "Draft" vs "Published" means everywhere in the CMS.

How this Help Center is organised

Each article follows the same shape: what it does, what to have ready, the steps, the fields, and what you should see when you're done. Destructive actions (delete, bulk delete) are always called out with a warning admonition before the steps that trigger them.

Toggle instead of delete

Almost every list in the CMS (products, sections, FAQs, menu items) has a "hide"/"active" toggle as well as a delete option. Prefer the toggle — it keeps the content in the system in case you want it back, without it showing on the live site. Delete is permanent.
